source.title: Embodied Representation Alignment with Mirror Neurons
source.authors: Wentao Zhu; Zhining Zhang; Yuwei Ren; Yin Huang; Hao Xu; Yizhou Wang

record.file_problem: The full paper and supplementary material are present. One internal figure reference appears as “??”.
record.tranche_reason: It measures alignment between separately trained action-understanding and embodied-execution models using a learned linear-projection retrieval probe. This bears on cross-model representational mapping, but does not reproduce a scale sweep or the original studies’ settings.
record.gate_note: The reported alignment results are the held-out retrieval probe in Figure 3 and the qualitative latent-space comparison in Figure 6. The action-recognition and robot-task performance tables and the Table 3 ablations measure task performance, not representational alignment, so they are not rows.
record.test_reason: The frozen-model probe tests linear alignability in a new setting: separately trained action-understanding and robotic-execution models. It bears on V4, although retrieval does not establish interchangeability with little task-performance loss.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the conclusion: the authors report spontaneous alignment between separately trained action-understanding and execution models, associated with task success, and improved task performance and representation quality after explicit joint alignment. Their common-reality explanation and proposed causal role for representation disentanglement remain interpretations rather than separately established results.
record.recipe_differences: Uses linear transformations, bidirectional contrastive learning, and held-out retrieval to probe action-understanding versus embodied-execution representations. It does not test model scaling or the original sources’ broader convergence claims.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported probe alignment varies with training progress and is higher for successful than failed execution samples. Table 3 varies positive-pair construction and temperature for task-performance evaluation, not for a reported alignment measurement.

fits_no_version.finding: Successful recognition and execution subsets have higher projected-representation retrieval alignment than failed subsets.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Action-understanding and robotic-execution representation alignment is associated with task success.

fits_no_version.finding: Explicit MN joint training produces qualitatively clearer same-instruction clustering and instruction separation in t-SNE visualizations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An explicit cross-task alignment objective can organize observed-action and executed-action representations into shared semantic clusters.

record.problems: The spontaneous-alignment evidence concerns one model pair and a learned linear probe. Exact Figure 3 subgroup and training-iteration values are not stated, and the probe results have no stated chance or other reference accuracy. The paper also does not compare mapped representations' task performance with an unmapped reference.
record.rows_left_out: Action-recognition and robot-task performance results in Tables 1 and 2, and the task-performance ablations in Table 3, are omitted because they do not measure representational alignment.

untested.parts: No model-size or capability sweep establishes increasing convergence with scale. Training progress alone does not establish this version.
No comparison of improving vision and language models on paired images and captions.
No comparison across initializations of the same architecture.
No replacement of one model's representations with another's, downstream loss measurement, layer stitching, relative representations, or mapping without paired supervision.
No identification of recurring interpretable features or circuits.
No comparison of alignment metrics, metric settings, or alignment under distribution shift. Table 3 measures task performance under different alignment-training choices.
No test of an alignment plateau or causal comparison separating shared data and objectives from a common-reality explanation. Incomplete retrieval alone does not establish this explanation.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text contains captions but no readable Figure 3 or Figure 6 graphics. No exact subgroup scores, retrieval chance baseline, or uncertainty estimates can be recovered. Learning probes on frozen models is distinct from explicitly training the underlying models to converge.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep of model size or capability, or comparison across independently trained models of varied architectures, objectives, and data.
No scaling test of vision-language alignment on paired images and captions. The study pairs action-understanding video representations with embodied-execution policy representations.
No comparison across random initializations of the same architecture or analysis of shared features or subspaces.

Tests learned linear projections and retrieval for one action-understanding/embodied-execution model pair. It does not test stitching, relative representations, unpaired mapping, or the amount of task-performance loss from mapping.
No recurring interpretable features or circuits are identified across models.
No comparison of representation-similarity metrics, settings such as neighbour count, or in-distribution versus out-of-distribution inputs.
No test of a plateau, the completeness of alignment, or whether shared training data/objectives rather than a common model of reality explain it.

rows.subject: ViCLIP [41] + ARP [44]
rows.stage_stated: separately trained; models frozen during alignment probing
rows.operation_detail: Fit two linear transformations with contrastive learning, then measure bidirectional nearest-neighbour retrieval on a held-out test set.

conditions.value: observed and executed actions sharing the same intent
alignment probe tracked over model training

rows.measure: Held-out average bidirectional nearest-neighbour retrieval accuracy for matching action representations
rows.value: More than 60%; the text says alignment rises rapidly in early training and reaches a high level.
rows.note: The text reports the >60% figure and trend; the graph does not provide readable exact values for individual training iterations. No chance or other reference accuracy is stated.
rows.check: The reported >60% held-out bidirectional Recall@1 demonstrates incomplete correspondence after learning two linear projections. It is not a measurement of representation replacement or downstream performance retained.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine for V4. Two learned linear projections yield more than 60% held-out average bidirectional Recall@1; representation substitution and downstream performance loss are not measured.
source_check.problem: Retrieval accuracy does not establish incomplete interchangeability; the reported lower bound also does not establish an upper limit on correspondence.

rows.subject: ViCLIP [41] + ARP [44]
rows.operation_detail: Measure projected-representation retrieval alignment for action-understanding samples split by recognition outcome.

conditions.value: correctly recognized versus incorrectly recognized samples
equal sample sizes for alignment probing

rows.measure: Representation alignment on the outcome-defined subsets
rows.note: The text describes experiments on correctly and incorrectly recognized samples, but does not state their separate values or clearly give the direction of this comparison.
rows.check: Section 2.3 describes higher alignment for task-successful subsets after discussing both recognition and execution. The record understates this qualitative direction, but separate recognition-subset scores are unavailable in the supplied text. The subgroup difference alone cannot establish interchangeability.

rows.subject: ViCLIP [41] + ARP [44]
rows.operation_detail: Measure projected-representation retrieval alignment for embodied-execution samples split by task outcome.

conditions.value: equal sample sizes for alignment probing

rows.measure: Representation alignment on the outcome-defined subsets
rows.value: figure only; the text states that alignment is significantly higher for successful than failed samples.
rows.uncertainty: Significance is stated, but no p-value or error estimate is given.
rows.note: The study reports the success-versus-failure direction in the text, but not separate numeric values.
rows.check: Higher retrieval alignment for successful than failed executions is explicitly reported, but this relative difference does not establish the absolute extent of mapping or little-loss interchangeability. The original observed state conflates the correlation with V4.

rows.subject: ViCLIP [41] + ARP [44], trained separately without the MN module
rows.operation_detail: Align representations into a shared latent space for t-SNE visualization.
rows.measure: Qualitative clustering of representations by instruction and model
rows.note: The text describes the MN approach as facilitating alignment; it gives no numeric comparison for this separately trained baseline.
rows.check: A t-SNE visualization of projected representations supplies neither a readable quantitative baseline nor a test of representation interchangeability.

rows.subject: ViCLIP [41] + ARP [44], jointly trained with the MN module
rows.operation_detail: Align representations into a shared latent space for t-SNE visualization.

conditions.value: joint training with the MN alignment objective

rows.measure: Qualitative clustering of representations by instruction and model
rows.value: The text describes same-instruction representations as clustering together and different instructions as forming distinct clusters.
rows.note: This alignment is trained explicitly; it is not evidence of spontaneous alignment in the absence of the MN objective.
rows.check: The models are explicitly trained to align, and qualitative clustering does not measure interchangeability. This is a method-analysis result, not evidence of independently arising convergence.

relationships.condition: Frozen, separately trained ViCLIP–ARP representations evaluated through learned linear projections
relationships.reason: r1 establishes partial linear correspondence: held-out matching-action retrieval exceeds 60%, rather than demonstrating nearly complete correspondence. This verdict concerns retrieval alignment; downstream interchangeability remains untested.
relationships.display_finding: Held-out matching-action retrieval exceeded 60% after linear projection, demonstrating partial correspondence without testing downstream interchangeability.
